messages:
leah_sales: quick heads-up — Swivel wants a POC to validate 1:1 API drop-in and prompt parity. kickoff call this afternoon, summarizing open items here.

omar_se: can you paste a minimal example of their request/response? i want to compare tokenization + function-calling semantics.

leah_sales: their sample (from support):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"swivel-large\",
  \"prompt\": \"Summarize the meeting notes:\",
  \"max_tokens\": 256
}
```
They return `outputs[0].text` in the response. They also mutate conversation state server-side on same request.

omar_se: Redwood responses use `choices[*].message` / streaming chunks and preserve explicit `conversation_id` in metadata. main diffs to check:
- response envelope (outputs vs choices)
- streaming behavior and early flush (they stream fewer chunks)
- function/tool calling shape (their `tool_call` vs our `tool_calls` array)

simon_infra: also watch KV-cache warmup. Swivel keeps session-level cache pinned to instance, which causes cold-start penalties on our multi-tenant config. for Dedicated we can pin but need to document perf and mem. latency baseline they expect: p99 < 400ms for 512 tokens. we should run end-to-end benchmark (local quantized build + hosted route).

nina_security: security checklist from enterprise: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, audit log retention 1y, IP allowlist, and data residency (EU). do we have SOC2 docs + pen test summary? ray_customer will likely ask for contract clause about non-production data retention.

ray_customer: yes — compliance is the blocker for legal. also asking about prompt-level redaction and the ability to opt-out of caching for specific requests.

omar_se: quick technical note on prompt parity: tokenizers differ (byte-level vs unicode-aware) -> prompt length/stop behavior can diverge. try this test pattern:
```
input = "\u201cQuote\u201d — some unicode chars"
// compare encoded length with Swivel vs Redwood tokenizer
```
If token offsets differ, completions can shift and stop sequences may not match. offer mapping doc + recommended prompt rewrites.

leah_sales: pricing/Qs from procurement: are committed-month discounts transferrable to Dedicated? and do we charge for prefix cache tokens? they want an estimate for 100M tokens/month and embeddings usage (10M vectors).

omar_se: short answers: hosted token pricing applies unless they sign Dedicated reserved capacity (different contract). prefix caching is not billed as extra tokens, but it affects compute footprint (we'll show cost model). embeddings billed per vector unit — we can simulate cost in the POC with sample workload.

simon_infra: operational note — if we enable pinned cache on Dedicated to match Swivel semantics, we need to provision + autoscale differently. I'll produce a runbook for the POC (gpu type, batch sizes, perf targets).

nina_security: also request: support for customer-managed JWK rotation and ability to rotate keys without downtime. need to confirm: do we support HSM-backed keys on Private?

leah_sales: ray_customer raised one more technical item: function-calling parity. they rely on deterministic args ordering. Swivel returns args as ordered list. Redwood outputs unordered dict sometimes (depending on model). can we provide an adapter shim to reorder fields?

omar_se: yes — we can ship a lightweight compatibility shim in front of the API that transforms `choices[*].message` -> `outputs[0].text` and normalizes `tool_call` -> `tool_calls` with ordered args. prototype snippet: 
```
// shim pseudocode
resp = call_redwood(req)
shim_out = { outputs: [{ text: resp.choices[0].message.content }] }
if (resp.tool_calls) shim_out.outputs[0].tool_call = normalize(resp.tool_calls[0])
return shim_out
```
works for POC but we should log transform latency.

dev-bot: NOTE: POC environment created: rg-poc-swivel-2026, creds shared in 1:1.

ray_customer: can you run 10 sample prompts (they sent a 50 prompt suite) and return diff rates where outputs differ > 5% on rouge/emd?

omar_se: yep — i'll run the suite against our tuned quantized model + their model. will post a small table.

leah_sales: next steps:
- omar -> run parity eval and post metrics (deadline: Tue EOD)
- simon -> POC infra runbook + perf numbers (deadline: Tue EOD)
- nina -> compile security packet + confirm HSM/KMS options (deadline: Wed)
- leah -> update commercial with estimated cost delta and draft contract language for caching/data clauses (Wed)

Any blockers? :eyes:

nina_security: only blocker is formal SOC2 + pen test timeline. we can run a compensating control during POC (read-only log export) but legal will still want reports.

ray_customer: sounds good — thanks team. we'll wait for the eval metrics before scheduling the legal call.

leah_sales: thanks all — i'll follow up with the call notes and attach the 50-prompt suite. :thumbsup:
